output.reason: missing_crs: the points layer states no CRS and its coordinates are projected (metres), while the zones are in geographic lon/lat. The points cannot be reliably put in the same CRS as the zones, so the within-join cannot be computed without guessing.
missing_features: the layer has no features named 'echo' or 'foxtrot'. The only names are alpha, bravo, charlie and delta.
missing_attribute: the layer has no 'station_code' field (features carry only 'name': alpha, bravo, charlie, delta), so stations ALX and BRV cannot be identified
invalid_distance_range: min_distance (10 km) is greater than max_distance (5 km), so no station can be both within 5 km and more than 10 km away

no_spatial_overlap: all points are in Berlin (lon 13.35-13.8, lat 52.42-52.55) while the zones cover Paris (lon 2.25-2.42, lat 48.8-48.9); no point lies within any zone, so the zone layer cannot assign zones to these points
inner spatial join, predicate=intersects (default); p4 lies on shared z1/z2 boundary so matches both; p5 matches no zone and is dropped
unknown_crs: EPSG:999999 is not a defined code in the EPSG registry, so the transformation target cannot be resolved
inner join with predicate contains; p4 is excluded because it lies on the shared boundary, and p5 is excluded because it is outside both zones

limitations: Small synthetic fixtures; they test operation correctness, not scale or real-world data quality.
Expected outputs come from one reference workflow (Shapely, pyproj, GEOS, PROJ); an error shared by those libraries would not be caught.
Tolerances are set per case and stated in explicit units, sized to catch the smallest error of the mistake each case targets; none is tighter than a correct answer given to 5 decimal places needs.
Rescored against gis_correctness 0.3.0 from saved outputs; previously scored against gis_correctness 0.2.0.

benchmark.notes: Every expected output is computed by reference.py; regenerate them with `geoevals bench regenerate gis_correctness`.
